analysis.investment_thesis: BlackBuck fails both Magic Formula screens decisively — Earnings Yield is a paltry ~0.8% (EBIT ₹93 Cr / EV ~₹11,267 Cr) and ROCE of 10.5% falls well below the 20% minimum threshold for a "good" business. The company has only just turned EBIT-positive in FY2025 after four consecutive years of operating losses, with no demonstrated track record of sustained high-return-on-capital economics.
key_strengths: High gross margins (74%) confirm a capital-light software platform model with pricing power potential
Finally EBITDA-positive (₹128 Cr in FY2025) with near-zero debt (D/E: 0.04) after aggressive deleveraging from ₹394 Cr borrowings in FY2021
Strong FII ownership (32.45%) signals institutional validation of the long-term B2B trucking platform thesis
key_risks: Revenue has contracted at -16.2% CAGR over 4 years (₹867 Cr in FY2021 → ₹427 Cr in FY2025) — even adjusting for business model shifts, absolute scale is deeply concerning
Earnings Yield of ~0.8% means the market is pricing in perfection; EV/EBITDA of 74x gives almost no margin of safety
Net profit still negative (-₹9 Cr in FY2025) and FCF generation is minimal (₹15 Cr) despite the EBITDA turn — not yet self-funding at scale
red_flags: 4-year revenue CAGR of -16.2% — a shrinking top line is a disqualifier for any growth premium
Operating CF erratic (3 of 5 years positive) and FY2025 investing CF of -₹467 Cr signals heavy capital deployment just as profitability is nascent
P/E of 29.5x shown despite ₹-9 Cr net profit — data inconsistency suggests the valuation is built on non-GAAP or very thin adjusted earnings, masking true economic loss
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on BlackBuck produces two failing grades. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV): EBIT of ₹93 Cr divided by Enterprise Value of ~₹11,267 Cr (₹11,333 Cr market cap + ₹38 Cr debt − ₹104 Cr cash) yields just 0.83% — I want to see at least 12–15% before I get interested. Return on Capital (ROCE per reported data): 10.5%, well short of the 20%+ floor for a "good" business. The business is structurally light on fixed assets (CWIP = zero, low capex), so the low ROIC reflects that not enough earnings have yet emerged relative to capital deployed — a profitability infancy problem, not a capital efficiency one.

The underlying platform story is directionally interesting — high gross margins (74%), near-zero debt, and finally positive EBIT in FY2025 suggest the unit economics can work. But the Magic Formula is not a story-investing framework. It demands proof, not promise. Four years of operating losses, a net loss still on the books in FY2025, and a P/S of 19x mean the market has already priced in a decade of successful execution. Greenblatt's system would not touch this until it demonstrates sustained ROIC above 20% for at least 2–3 consecutive years — and trades at a meaningful earnings yield. At current prices, all upside is in the price and all risk is in the execution.
